relays_verified.notes: Accepts anon kind 1, 40, 42 (OK:true, empty msg). Read-back of kind 42 via fresh REQ confirmed. GOTCHA: intermittently returns HTTP 503 at the WebSocket upgrade under load (hit once, worked on retry ~10s later) — client needs reconnect with backoff. connect=1060ms, publish->OK=481ms, REQ->EVENT=523ms.
Cleanest relay of the survey. Accepts anon kind 1, 40, 42; instant read-back on fresh REQ. connect=642ms, publish->OK=143ms, REQ->EVENT=143ms. Primary recommendation.

SHADOW ACCEPT — returns ["OK",id,true,""] for anon kind 42 but the event is silently dropped: not retrievable by id, author, or #e (verified twice with two different keys). Kind 1 and kind 40 ARE stored and served. Do NOT count its OK:true toward kind-42 durability. connect=626ms, publish->OK=156ms.

Accepts anon kind 1 and kind 40 (stored + served), but rejects anon kind 42 with ["OK",id,false,"not acceptable at this point (8)"] — consistent across brand-new and previously-seen pubkeys (strfry write-policy plugin). Usable as a read/backup relay for kind 40, useless for chat messages. connect=681ms, publish->OK=190ms.

Fastest connect (312ms) and accepts anon kind 1 + kind 40, but rejects anon kind 42 with ["OK",id,false,"Policy violated and pubkey is not in our web of trust."] — explicit WoT gate on chat kinds, regardless of key history.
UNREACHABLE — WebSocket opening handshake timed out on two separate attempts (15-20s). Excluded entirely.
HTTP 403 at the WebSocket upgrade itself — paid/NIP-42-auth relay, rejects anonymous connections before any Nostr frame is exchanged. Excluded (as anticipated in the task).

(wss://relay.damus.io returned HTTP 503 at the WS upgrade on this first fresh attempt; re-run ~10s later on another fresh socket returned the same EVENT + EOSE — so fresh-REQ read-back confirmed on BOTH damus and primal. A second kind-42 published later read back on both as ["msg2","msg1"] — newest-first ordering.)
gotchas: OK:true is NOT durability. wss://nostr.mom ACKed anonymous kind-42 with ["OK",id,true,""] then silently dropped it — unreachable by id, author, or #e query minutes later (reproduced with two different keys). The site must count a relay as 'delivered' only if the event later appears in a REQ, or simply only trust relays empirically proven to serve kind 42 (damus + primal).

Relay policy is PER-KIND: nos.lol and offchain.pub happily accept anonymous kind 1 (probe stored + served) but reject anonymous kind 42 — nos.lol: 'not acceptable at this point (8)', offchain.pub: 'Policy violated and pubkey is not in our web of trust.' Both rejections are stable across brand-new and previously-seen pubkeys. Never generalize a kind-1 survey to chat kinds.

Only 2 of 7 candidate relays (relay.damus.io, relay.primal.net) both accept AND serve anonymous kind 42. Publish chat messages to those two plus nostr.mom (free extra copy of kind 40/1, zero-cost lottery ticket for 42), read from damus + primal. Total redundancy for chat messages is 2 — the UI should tolerate one being down.

Reconnect etiquette: damus intermittently refuses the WebSocket upgrade with HTTP 503 (load shedding) — the browser fires a bare 'error'+'close'. Reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter (e.g. 1s,2s,4s..30s cap); a retry ~10s later succeeded. relay.nostr.band never completed a handshake from this network; nostr.wine 403s anonymous connections at HTTP level (paid/NIP-42) — drop both.

Dedupe by event id across relays: the same event arrives once per relay you're subscribed to; keep a Set of seen ids before rendering. Sharp edge observed: two INDEPENDENTLY signed events collided to the SAME id because pubkey/kind/tags/content matched and created_at fell in the same second (ids are deterministic; only sigs differed) — id-dedupe handles this correctly, just don't key UI state on sig.

EOSE semantics: every surveyed relay sends ["EOSE",subid] after replaying stored events; live events continue on the same subscription afterward. Use EOSE to (a) stop the loading spinner, (b) switch from batch-insert to append mode. Don't wait for EOSE from ALL relays — one is enough; others may be slow or return nothing.

Ordering: limit-bounded REQs return stored events NEWEST-FIRST (observed on damus and primal: [msg2,msg1]). Re-sort ascending by created_at client-side, tiebreak by id (created_at has 1s resolution, ties are routine in a live chat).

created_at freshness: use Math.floor(Date.now()/1000). Relays enforce skew windows (typically reject >~15 min future / very old past). A visitor with a wrong system clock will get OK:false or silent drops — if publishes fail on all relays, surface a 'check your clock' hint. Also never send float timestamps: the id serialization would differ between signer and verifier.

OK vs NOTICE vs AUTH: ["OK",event_id,bool,message] is the per-EVENT ack — match on event id, treat missing OK after ~10s as failure (timeout observed nowhere on healthy relays; publish->OK was 60-481ms). ["NOTICE",msg] is connection-level free text, never an ack — log it, don't parse it. ["AUTH",challenge] (NIP-42) may arrive unsolicited; anonymous chat ignores it (auth relays were excluded).

NIP-01 id serialization sharp edges: hash the UTF-8 BYTES (TextEncoder) of JSON.stringify([0,pubkey,created_at,kind,tags,content]). JS JSON.stringify natively produces NIP-01-compliant escaping: only ", \, and control chars <0x20 escaped (\n stays the two-char sequence backslash-n; emoji/CJK/accents stay RAW UTF-8, never \uXXXX). pubkey must be lowercase hex. Verified byte-exact against nostr-tools both directions incl. content with newlines, quotes, backslashes, tabs, ✓, 中文, and surrogate-pair emoji.

Rate limits: none triggered at survey pace (single events, seconds apart). nos.lol's '(8)' is a policy-plugin code, not rate limiting. Do not blind-retry an OK:false — the same event will be rejected again; only retry transport failures. Site should throttle sends client-side (e.g. 1 msg/2s) to stay under strfry per-IP burst limits.

Max content length: untested at the limit (chat probes were short); typical relay caps are on total event JSON (~64-100KB strfry default). Cap chat input at ~1000 chars — far below any relay limit and right for UX.

Subscriptions: use unique REQ subscription ids per purpose, CLOSE ones you're done with (["CLOSE",subid]); relays cap concurrent subs per connection. One long-lived sub {kinds:[42],"#e":[CHANNEL_ID],limit:50} is all the chat needs.

Bundle env note: nostr-crypto.js needs globalThis.crypto (all browsers have it; Node 18 lab tests need --experimental-global-webcrypto). randomPrivateKey() throws without it — fine for the site, relevant only to Node-based CI.

Channel provenance: kind-40 creator burner privkey is preserved at nostr-lab/channel.json (burner_privkey_hex) in scratch ONLY — if you ever want to publish a kind-41 channel-metadata update it must be signed by that key. If scratch is wiped, the channel metadata is frozen forever (fine for this joke; the channel id keeps working regardless).
